tldr: Midday batch, Aug 16: OpenAI's new enterprise report quantifies the agent gap — frontier firms use plugins 2x and skills 6x more than typical organizations. Anthropic's Dario Amodei pushes back on 'doom-heavy' AI messaging by betting on biology and medicine as the upside proof case, saying the thing that will work is actually curing cancer. Science's drug-discovery blog takes stock of where AI really stands in pharma (113-pt HN story, citing a Nature Reviews piece), and a top HN essay argues working with AI now feels more like leadership than coding (269 pts, 174 comments).

articles.title: OpenAI Quantifies the Enterprise Agent Gap: Plugins 2x, Skills 6x
articles.summary: New 'How Enterprises Put AI to Work' report: the top 10% of enterprises use plugins twice as often and skills six times as often as typical firms — hard numbers on the agentic-workflow adoption gap.

articles.title: Dario Amodei: Anthropic Ramps Biology and Medicine as AI's Proof Case
articles.summary: Rejecting 'doom-heavy' messaging critiques, Dario says the upside proof case is actually curing cancer — Anthropic is ramping biology/medicine work fast; expect more bio/health launches.

articles.title: AI in Drug Discovery: Where It Stands and the Path Forward
articles.summary: Science's drug-discovery blog takes stock of AI's real impact in pharma, anchored on a new Nature Reviews article (113 HN points, 57 comments).

articles.title: Working with AI Feels More Like Leadership Than Coding
articles.summary: Top HN essay (269 pts, 174 comments): as models do the mechanics, the human job shifts to direction, review and delegation — working with AI is leadership work, not typing.
